modules.title: Design secure access to AWS resources

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Who secures what, and how should the account root user be handled?

reveal.text: AWS secures the infrastructure that runs AWS services. Customers secure what they run and configure in AWS, including identities, data, network controls, operating systems where applicable, and application settings. Protect the AWS account root user with MFA, avoid routine root use, and use least-privilege identities for day-to-day administration.

prompts.label: TASK MAP
prompts.placeholder: Reveal each row and compare neighboring architecture choices.

cells.best_for: AWS secures the cloud infrastructure, while customers secure their data, identities, configurations, and workloads in the cloud.
IAM authorization evaluates applicable identity and resource policies, and an explicit Deny overrides an Allow.
IAM roles provide temporary credentials and are commonly assumed through AWS STS instead of using long-term access keys.
AWS IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce access to multiple AWS accounts and applications by using federated identities and permission sets.
AWS Organizations groups accounts, SCPs set permission guardrails, and AWS Control Tower helps establish and govern a multi-account landing zone.
Resource-based policies attach to supported AWS resources and can name principals that are allowed or denied access.
A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions that an IAM user or role can receive from identity-based policies.

prompts.label: ROOT USER HYGIENE
prompts.placeholder: Which practices should you remember?

cells.remember: Use only for tasks that require root credentials; not for routine administration.
Protect root access with MFA and secure recovery mechanisms.
Do not create root access keys for normal automation; use roles and temporary credentials.
Use federated or role-based access with least privilege.

nodes.title: IAM roles, STS, and cross-account access

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: IAM roles provide temporary credentials and are commonly assumed through AWS STS instead of using long-term access keys.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When are roles and STS the strong clue?

items: A workload needs AWS API access without stored long-term keys: use an IAM role and temporary credentials.
One account needs controlled access to another: assume a cross-account role through AWS STS.

reveal.text: A subnet is public when its route table provides a path to an internet gateway; private application and database tiers normally avoid direct inbound internet paths.

prompts.label: TASK MAP

cells.best_for: A subnet is public when its route table provides a path to an internet gateway; private application and database tiers normally avoid direct inbound internet paths.
Security groups are stateful controls attached to resources such as ENIs, while network ACLs are stateless controls applied at the subnet boundary.
VPC endpoints provide private access to supported services without requiring traffic to traverse an internet gateway or NAT gateway.
AWS Secrets Manager stores sensitive credentials and supports controlled retrieval and automated rotation for supported secret types.
AWS WAF filters HTTP and HTTPS requests with web ACL rules, while AWS Shield provides managed protection against distributed denial-of-service attacks.
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity, Inspector identifies software and network exposure vulnerabilities, Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, and Security Hub aggregates security findings.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: AWS KMS creates and controls KMS keys used to protect data. Every KMS key has a key policy, which is the primary resource policy controlling who can administer or use the key.

prompts.label: TASK MAP
prompts.placeholder: Reveal each row and compare neighboring architecture choices.

cells.best_for: AWS KMS creates and controls encryption keys that AWS services can use to protect data at rest.
AWS Certificate Manager provisions and manages TLS certificates for supported integrated AWS services.
Amazon S3 combines IAM and bucket policies with features such as versioning, lifecycle rules, replication, and Object Lock to control access and protect object data.
Backups create recoverable copies, while replication maintains additional copies in another location for availability, locality, or disaster-recovery objectives.
Data classification identifies sensitive or regulated information so that access, encryption, retention, and monitoring controls can match the data's requirements.

prompts.label: KEY POLICY
prompts.placeholder: Why can an IAM allow still be insufficient?

reveal.text: A key policy is attached to the KMS key. It must allow the access directly or enable the account to delegate access through IAM policies. Cross-account KMS access must account for both key-side permission and caller-side IAM permission.

prompts.label: KEY ROTATION
prompts.placeholder: What should you remember about rotation?

reveal.text: Eligible customer managed symmetric KMS keys can use automatic or on-demand rotation. Rotation changes key material while AWS KMS retains older material needed to decrypt existing ciphertext.

nodes.title: S3 access, versioning, lifecycle, and Object Lock

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Amazon S3 combines IAM and bucket policies with features such as versioning, lifecycle rules, replication, and Object Lock to control access and protect object data.

prompts.label: READ THE CONFIG

annotations.title: Deny insecure requests
annotations.explanation: The statement blocks requests that match the insecure-transport condition.

annotations.title: Require TLS
annotations.explanation: The condition detects requests that are not using secure transport.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: S3 access, versioning, lifecycle, and Object Lock

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: An S3 feature that keeps multiple versions of an object so earlier versions can be recovered.
A period during which protected data must be kept and cannot be removed under the configured control.
Write once, read many. Data can be read after writing but not changed during the protected period.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Backups create recoverable copies, while replication maintains additional copies in another location for availability, locality, or disaster-recovery objectives.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When do you need backup vs replication?

items: Use backups to restore an earlier known-good state after deletion, corruption, or another failure.
Use replication to maintain an additional copy for availability, locality, or disaster recovery.
Replication is not automatically a substitute for historical backup because a bad change can also be replicated.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

glossary.definition: A stored backup state that can be used to restore data or a resource to an earlier point.
Recovery point objective. The maximum recent data loss a design is intended to tolerate, measured in time.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Data classification identifies sensitive or regulated information so encryption, access, retention, monitoring, and handling controls can match the data. Amazon Macie is the AWS-service clue when the requirement is to discover sensitive data in Amazon S3.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: What scenario strongly points to Macie?

items: Use Macie when the company needs to discover PII, credentials, financial data, or other sensitive information stored in S3.
Do not map every generic data-classification requirement to Macie; the strong AWS-service clue is sensitive-data discovery in S3.
